fields.position: Integral DeltaNet retains a fast delta state and a historical integral state, with key-channel integration/readout gates. The integral state does not feed back into the delta update.
fields.tradeoff: KRA maintains regression coefficients and posterior covariance, restoring writable uncertainty under forgetting. Integral instead stores a delta state and its weighted history. Covariance is not a memory copy, and integral history does not implement KRA covariance-guided interference correction. Local L1 cannot compare language recall.

fields.title: Integral DeltaNet: Improved Linear Attention with Adaptive Memory Integration
fields.body: KRA maintains regression coefficients and posterior covariance, restoring writable uncertainty under forgetting. Integral instead stores a delta state and its weighted history. Covariance is not a memory copy, and integral history does not implement KRA covariance-guided interference correction. Local L1 cannot compare language recall. The first equation is GDN-2; broadcasting one beta across erase/write gives KDA. Lambda and gamma act on key channels, not value rows or one scalar. Integrate the updated S. The paper uses rank128 gates initialized near lambda=1-gamma=1/1024; the local rank is reduced but the trainable parameterization is retained.

fields.question: Why is KRA covariance P not an integral state?
fields.answer: P represents uncertainty and changes writes; X stores weighted S history and only participates in readout. Their semantics and updates differ.
fields.example: Illustration:KRA forgetting can restore P without a new value,whereas X remains retained S history,not a write-gain matrix.

fields.position: DeCo estimates per-head principal subspaces at runtime and appends Q-side/K-side first-order residual projections as extra quantized channels of one expanded dot product.
fields.tradeoff: DualQuant fits row/column scales from static weights and rescales activations. DeCo estimates a basis from current Q/K and compensates both rounding residuals. Neither floating simulation is a packed low-bit kernel; A100 floating execution cannot establish native FP4 acceleration.

fields.title: DeCo-Attention: Decompose to Compensate for Low-Precision Attention
fields.body: DualQuant fits row/column scales from static weights and rescales activations. DeCo estimates a basis from current Q/K and compensates both rounding residuals. Neither floating simulation is a packed low-bit kernel; A100 floating execution cannot establish native FP4 acceleration. Eq6 uses raw rotated sampled Q/K,not already-rounded operands; normalize each Gram by its own trace. Sample max(N/256,2r),with stratification for mixed text/audio/video. Eq25 uses a power-of-two group scale,unsigned E4M3 block scales per16channels,and E2M1 values,including compensation channels. Divide scores by original sqrt(d),not sqrt(d+2r).

fields.question: Can DeCo replace DualQuant's scale solver?
fields.answer: No. DualQuant optimizes static-weight row/column reconstruction scales; DeCo corrects dynamic attention Q/K residuals.
fields.example: Illustration:two prompts change Q/K and the estimated DeCo basis,while static weight scales can be reused.

fields.position: Given a fixed/versioned scalar scorer, cancel exact-identity report coefficients before acquisition and separate mean from ordinary-covariance support. Local code is CPU exact arithmetic, not model generation or judging.
fields.tradeoff: Probabilistic Autorater targets calibrated preference probabilities and proper rewards. CAFA leaves the scorer unchanged and reduces required scores. Exact recovery does not make a judge correct; fewer inputs do not establish lower total workflow cost.

fields.title: Evaluation-budget optimization must fix both the requested statistic and scorer version
fields.body: Re-reading Probabilistic Autorater confirms that numerical proper rewards/parsing are not a generative judge capability. CAFA likewise requires an external scorer, while its defining fixed-bank algorithm can execute exactly. Mean support uses across-draw coefficient sums; ordinary covariance retains any identity with a nonzero draw coefficient. Mirror contrasts can have zero mean but positive variance. Cache keys must separate rubric/deployment versions; semantic identity merging and zero imputation are invalid. Feedback savings do not calibrate a judge, and workflow changes in sampler/draw budgets are not all attributable to fixed-bank cancellation.

fields.question: If a bank's mean needs no scores, can its confidence interval also be recovered without scores?
fields.answer: No. Ordinary covariance needs per-draw vectors, which may remain variable after mean cancellation. Interpreting intervals additionally requires sampling independence and a coverage procedure, excluding repeated judge noise.
fields.example: Teaching example: differences3/-3 have mean zero and sample variance18. Without the scores, mean cancellation is known but that variance is not; zero uncertainty cannot be asserted.

fields.summary: Re-read Probabilistic Autorater against fixed-v1 CAFA Eqs.2–4/Algorithm2. Added calibration versus acquisition planning, mean/covariance support, versioned caching, non-imputation and fixed-bank versus population-uncertainty boundaries. CAFA is CPU-only; full LLM/judge experiments are high-cost review DONE.

fields.position: Extrapolate frozen initial early/final distributions of a native looped model and directly distill the standard final loop with exact reverse KL, without external teachers/reference answers. Local scope is supplied-logit math only.
fields.tradeoff: LoOPSD searches repeated-layer routes in ordinary models, validates teachers and alternates refresh. ELPSD has no route search and keeps its extrapolated teacher frozen. The separately named LoopOPD is not existing LoOPSD; a shared KL form does not equate teacher construction or sampling.

fields.title: Extra-compute views differ between route search, loop readouts and extrapolated targets
fields.body: The current LoOPSD README defines a teacher through repeated-interval search/validation while students use the standard path; it is not the separately named LoopOPD in ELPSD. ELPSD reads early/final loops in one frozen forward of a native four-loop model and trains its final loop. Weight zero degenerates at initialization. Idealized refresh with a fixed early loop compounds log-odds by1+w, so LoOPSD's refresh cannot be copied mechanically. Response-balanced gradients and moving-target controls execute no looped model, route selection or on-policy sampler, and do not reopen deferred high-cost work.

fields.question: Why not give ELPSD the alternating teacher refresh used by LoOPSD?
fields.answer: Teacher construction differs. LoOPSD re-searches and validates repeated-layer routes. Refreshing ELPSD from its current final loop repeatedly amplifies a direction under the paper's fixed-early-loop exact-fit idealization, removing the fixed target.
fields.example: Teaching example: three idealized refreshes atw0.5 multiply relative log-odds by3.375, unlike independently validating a new repeated-layer route.

fields.summary: Re-read LoOPSD against fixed-v1 ELPSD Section3/AppendixA. Distinguished route search, fixed loop extrapolation and LoOPSD/LoopOPD naming; added zero-weight degeneration, idealized-refresh limits and response-balanced reduction. CPU supplied-logit components only; full8-GPU training is high-cost review DONE, with no reopening of old plans.

fields.position: Authenticate original user text before policy synthesis using ingress witnesses, an ordered complete commitment and current count. The agent's summary context supplies no authority.
fields.tradeoff: RuntimeTickets checks recipient/object/budget before effects; its audit HMAC chain does not establish prefix completeness. Current-count checks reject omitted cancellations here but supply neither object validators nor semantic policy safety.

fields.title: Authenticated origins do not replace semantic authorization or effect contracts
fields.body: Separate agent summaries from authenticated authorizer input. Occurrence MACs, ordered commitments and current-count/fresh-boundary checks jointly close echo, replay and omission gaps. Persistent-counter tests assume protected keys/state/issuance; SQLite is not agent isolation. RuntimeTickets freezes host-restricting effect contracts, audits before callbacks and avoids retries under uncertainty, but its local chain does not prove complete prefixes. The layers compose without local LLM attack-rate evidence. The full multi-model/live matrix is terminally not reproduced for cost.

fields.question: Does this gate protect the same boundary as RuntimeTickets?
fields.answer: No. It protects authorization input before policy synthesis; RuntimeTickets checks frozen recipient/object/budget contracts before effects. Intact originals do not prove correct policy semantics or authenticate summaries through valid sends.
fields.example: Teaching example: a generator can still broaden recipients after reading authentic text, requiring effect-level ticket checks rather than treating MACs as semantic understanding.

fields.position: Before gains are observed, fixed-domain categorical policies allocate rho, round to exactly Q queries, obtain only selected marginals and execute IPW/KL updates.
fields.tradeoff: OOAS sees aggregate task feedback and turn hints under shared exponential noise/whole-task same-arm events. This paper can query counterfactual coordinates; denominators, feedback granularity and FTRL/KL updates are not interchangeable.

fields.title: Unbiased budgeted feedback depends on the sampling event, not a generic 1/p trick
fields.body: SubMAPL rho denotes inclusion marginals: fixed-cardinality dependent rounding must preserve E[Z]=rho, and querying cannot inspect current gains or sampled joint actions. IPW precedes per-agent KL ascent; square-root allocation optimizes a second-moment bound, not success rates. OOAS shared noise makes whole-task same-arm probability differ from products of marginals and assigns no residual after switching. Both local entries are finite mathematical kernels, not LLM agents. SubMAPL migration/environment are unaccepted without high-cost evidence, so full status remains scope-limited with false full review rather than a fabricated cost-DONE terminal.

fields.question: Can SubMAPL and OOAS interchange importance weights?
fields.answer: No. SubMAPL observes queried counterfactual marginals and corrects coordinate inclusion; OOAS sees task aggregates and corrects hint residuals by a shared-noise whole-task same-arm event. Feedback and updates differ.
fields.example: Teaching example: switching arms zeroes OOAS residual attribution, while two queried SubMAPL coordinates still receive their own inclusion-corrected updates.

fields.position: The L1 component implements a small dual encoder/decoder with dot-product prediction, unit-Gaussian reparameterization and slot-level augmentation for Equations3–7/Algorithm1. Callers provide bucket IDs or embedded floating slots; no production features or true stable factors are read. Slot selection, independent slot masking and element-mean MSE are explicit local choices. Complete field embedding/dropout grouping, chronological incremental training, MMoE, private ranking and public benchmark comparisons are absent.
fields.tradeoff: COTTI uses a differentiable CPC gate for regular/promotional-view consistency, history-distance RW weights and serving-time ABA calibration. ELBO-TDS instead constrains stable factors through a multi-view Gaussian prior and input reconstruction, leaving supervised prediction on original observations; it has no ABA-style serving probability correction. Both rely on stable-semantics assumptions. Alignment or reconstruction does not establish causal identifiability, and different production A/B experiments do not establish a head-to-head winner.

fields.summary: ELBO-TDS assumes short-term fluctuations around relatively stable user/item factors. It does more than align augmented representations: unit-variance encoder posteriors are reparameterized, decoders retain individual features, and cross-view priors suppress transient noise. Task prediction uses deterministic means from original observations. Statistical buckets are perturbed locally, sequence inputs masked and categorical embeddings dropped, gated by global feature selection.
